original_question: Is every minimal field algebraically closed, where an infinite field K is called minimal when every subset A of K definable by a first-order formula in the language of rings is finite or cofinite?
target_in_paper: The draft does not match arXiv:1106.1310, which is "Open Problems in the Theory of Ample Fields" rather than a paper on minimal fields. The statement your draft is trying to capture is the official Podewski-conjecture formulation: Conjecture 1, "Each minimal field is algebraically closed," from the Podewski-conjecture paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.1310))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the main conjecture itself and the core finite/cofinite idea behind minimality for an infinite field. It is very close to the paper's official formulation. ([math.uni.wroc.pl](https://www.math.uni.wroc.pl/~kkrup/minifield3.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper's notion of minimality is definability with parameters; saying only "definable by a first-order formula in the language of rings" is incomplete unless parameters from K are allowed. ([math.uni.wroc.pl](https://www.math.uni.wroc.pl/~kkrup/minifield3.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The ambient structure is the pure field structure (equivalently, the field viewed in the ring language), not an arbitrary expansion by extra predicates or orders. ([math.uni.wroc.pl](https://www.math.uni.wroc.pl/~kkrup/minifield3.pdf?utm_source=openai))

For a fully stand-alone statement, it helps to spell out that "cofinite" means that the complement in K is finite. ([math.uni.wroc.pl](https://www.math.uni.wroc.pl/~kkrup/minifield3.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The nearby paper context shows that the unordered/symmetric case is already proved, and the remaining difficulty is the ordered/non-symmetric case via Proposition 1.1 and Theorem 1; however, that reduction is context, not part of the conjecture's official wording. ([math.uni.wroc.pl](https://www.math.uni.wroc.pl/~kkrup/minifield3.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Must every infinite field K, regarded as a pure field, be algebraically closed whenever every subset of K definable with parameters in the language of rings is either finite or cofinite?
justification: The nearest paper-faithful target is the official conjecture itself, not a broader model-theoretic variant and not the paper's reduction to ordered/non-symmetric cases. In the introduction, the paper states Conjecture 1 exactly as "Each minimal field is algebraically closed." Proposition 1.1 provides the symmetric/non-symmetric dichotomy for minimal structures with definable generic type, and Theorem 1 settles the unordered/symmetric side; this confirms that your draft is aiming at the main conjecture rather than at the reduction conjecture or the almost-linear special case. The only substantive sharpening needed to make your draft fully stand-alone is to add that definability is with parameters and that the field is considered in the pure field language. ([math.uni.wroc.pl](https://www.math.uni.wroc.pl/~kkrup/minifield3.pdf?utm_source=openai))
